body:
> From the third-pass review of PR #190 (#185, merged 2026-08-29). Neither blocked the merge.

## What

1. **Memoise the beat date by sha** (`src/dispatch.js` ~618, the idle-threshold `lockBeatAt` read): a commit's date is immutable and `listLocks` already hands the tick the sha, so keep `sha → date` in `state` and read the commit only when the ref moved. Today: +1 `GET /git/commits/<sha>` per tick per pidless attempt once its run-comment signal is 20 min old, for the rest of its life; and two reads per tick in the window where both the idle read and the `stale_after` read fire for the same sha (probe h). Test: two ticks, unchanged ref → one read.
2. **Boot-time guard on `livePid`** (`src/dispatch.js` ~601): `pidFileStale(at, { uptime })` exists (`src/model.js` ~1164) but is used for pid files only. After a reboot a reused pid makes a dead attempt hold its paths until the 60-min `stale_after` reclaim — where the old timing rule released it — and that reclaim then SIGTERMs `a.pid` unguarded (the reviewer's probe j killed its own probe process). Gate: `!pidFileStale(a.started_at, { uptime: os.uptime() }) && pidAlive(a.pid)` for `livePid`, and the same guard on the `crashed` check and on `failAttempt`'s kill.
3. Nit: `test/model.test.js` ~124 assertion strings still say "inside/past one tick interval".

## Done when

- Fake-gh test: unchanged lock ref across two ticks → one commit read; moved ref → a second read.
- A pid attempt whose `started_at` predates boot is treated as not live (holds nothing, is not signalled); a live-after-boot pid still holds.
- `npm run lint && npm test` green.
goal: The idle rule costs no repeated commit reads for an unchanged lock ref, and a pid reused after a reboot neither holds paths nor gets SIGTERMed by the reclaim
title: Idle rule follow-ups: memoise the lock-beat date by sha, and guard livePid (and the reclaim kill) against a pid reused after reboot
